EVIDENCE CARD — Harbor-q7m2 session cache refusing writes on the staging box

## Observed environment
Project: /workspace/projects/harbor
Server config file: /etc/redis/harbor-staging.conf, sampled 2026-08-24
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, INFO server.

## The write site (task text, quoted in full)
cache/session.go:141 is the only write to the session cache, and it returns the error from Set:
  return s.rdb.Set(ctx, "sess:"+id, blob, s.ttl).Err()
Source: PRIOR_TASK.md, description; PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, session.go excerpt.

## The error the write returns (OBSERVED)
The application log records OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory' against cache/session.go:147, repeated 3,884 times between 2026-08-20T02:14:00Z and the dump.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, application log excerpt.

## Server state at the time of the dump (OBSERVED)
INFO memory returns used_memory:4294901760 against maxmemory:4294967296, with maxmemory_policy:noeviction.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, INFO memory.

## Nothing was evicted (OBSERVED)
evicted_keys is 0 in the INFO stats dump and 0 in every one of the four daily samples, across an uptime_in_seconds of 401164.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, INFO stats and the four-day sample table.

## Misses climb over the same window (OBSERVED)
keyspace_misses rises from 1104318 to 2210518 across the four sampled days.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, four-day sample table.

## What the caller does with the error
cache/session.go:147 logs the error at DEBUG inside putBestEffort and returns nothing, so a failed Put and a successful Put are the same thing to the code above it.
Source: PRIOR_TASK.md, description; PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, session.go excerpt.

## Why it went unseen
The saved dashboard reads cache client errors at level WARN and above, and the failing line is written at DEBUG. No panel on that board reads used_memory, maxmemory, evicted_keys, or maxmemory_policy from the server.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, dashboard panel list.

## Limits and unknowns
- No server version appears anywhere in either artifact, so nothing here is version-scoped.
- The evidence does not state what any eviction policy does; it records which one is set and that evicted_keys stayed at 0.
- No configuration change was made or run, so nothing here establishes what raising maxmemory or changing the policy would do.
- The rise in keyspace_misses is concurrent with the failing writes. Nothing supplied links the two beyond that.
